preview.label: Preview
preview.engineDown: The video engine (libobs) did not start. Check the log.

tracking.label: Face tracking
tracking.cameraDenied: No permission to use the camera. Check Windows Settings → Privacy → Camera.
tracking.cameraBusy: The camera is being used by another program (Zoom, Teams, the Camera app…). Close it and try again.

errors.engine_not_running: The video engine is not running.
errors.calibration_no_face: Your face was not seen during calibration. Improve the light, face the camera and try again.
errors.calibration_eyes: No difference was detected between open and closed eyes. Try again and keep your eyes fully closed between the two beeps.
errors.calibration_mouth: An open mouth was not detected. Try again and open it as wide as you can.
errors.calibration_invalid: The calibration values are not valid. Please repeat it.

tooltips.loadAvatar: 3D avatars in VRM format (version 0.x or 1.0). Keep them in the recursos\avatares folder. Don’t have one? Create it for free with VRoid Studio.
tooltips.tracking: Uses your webcam so the avatar copies your head, eyes and mouth. Everything is processed on your device: the video never leaves your computer.
tooltips.fps: How many times per second your face is analyzed. Above 25 looks smooth; if it drops, add more light in front of you.
tooltips.values: What the camera measures, from 0 to 1. Mouth: 0 = closed, 1 = wide open. Eyes: 0 = open, 1 = closed. Use it to tune blinking and the mouth (user guide, section 7).
tooltips.lipsync: Will move the avatar’s mouth with your voice, using the microphone. Coming soon.
tooltips.expression: Shortcut {shortcut}: works even when avat-os is not in the foreground. Press it again to go back to neutral. Some avatars block blinking or the mouth with certain expressions.
tooltips.neutral: Clears the active expression and returns to the normal face.
tooltips.background: Background behind the avatar. It is transparent for now; soon you will be able to use a color or an image (PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF; ideally 1920×1080).
tooltips.comingSoon: Still under construction: coming in a future version.
tooltips.calibrate: Tunes blinking, the mouth and your straight-ahead pose to your face and camera. Requires face tracking to be on. It is saved for next time.
tooltips.calibrationStart: Takes about 15 seconds. During the eyes step two beeps will guide you, because you won’t be able to see the screen.
tooltips.calibrationReset: Deletes your calibration and goes back to the default values.
tooltips.avatarStatus: The avatar is drawn in OBS’s built-in browser. The first time, or when the computer is very busy (for example right after compiling), it can take up to a minute to appear.
tooltips.calibrationAdjust: Change eye and mouth sensitivity without repeating the calibration, with a live preview on the avatar.
tooltips.eyeSensitivity: More: the avatar closes its eyes sooner and fully with a soft blink. Less: you need to close them more (useful if the avatar squints by itself).
tooltips.mouthSensitivity: More: the mouth opens wider with little movement (if you talk with your mouth almost closed). Less: it opens less (if it looks exaggerated).

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.intro: Tune tracking to your face and camera in 3 short steps. Sit as you do when streaming, with good light.
calibration.neutral: Step 1 of 3: look straight at the screen, eyes open and mouth closed.
calibration.eyes: Step 2 of 3: when you hear the beep, close your eyes and keep them closed until the second beep.
calibration.mouth: Step 3 of 3: open your mouth as wide as you can.
calibration.adjustHelp: Blink and talk: the avatar already uses these values. If you don’t like it, move the sliders; changes apply instantly and are not saved until you press Save.
calibration.legend: Bar = what the camera measures now. Gray mark = starts closing (or opening); white mark = fully.
